children: Blue Origin has raised $10 billion in its first financing round involving outside investors, valuing Jeff Bezos’s space company at about $140 billion, The Wall Street Journal reported Thursday.

Bezos is contributing another $2 billion to the round, bringing his total investment in Blue Origin to roughly $30 billion since founding the company in 2000. The financing could ultimately exceed the initial $10 billion target.
The fundraising offers a rare valuation for privately held Blue Origin and gives the company additional capital to challenge SpaceX

across rocket launches, satellites and government space programs. It also provides a glimpse at ambitious financial targets: Blue Origin generated about $800 million in revenue in 2025 and expects $1.4 billion this year, with projections exceeding $30 billion by 2030.

Blue Origin employs about 15,000 people and is betting heavily on its reusable New Glenn rocket. The company has completed three New Glenn missions, though launches have been suspended since a vehicle exploded on a Florida launchpad in May.

Future growth is expected to come from launch services, a planned satellite communications business and an AI satellite network, putting Blue Origin into increasingly direct competition with Elon Musk’s SpaceX.
